confidence_note: Book text read. Presented as a reflection ('if you are a poet'), not a scene with a listener; no invented dialogue.
facts: 'If you are a poet, you will see clearly that there is a cloud floating in this sheet of paper.' Without a cloud no rain; without rain trees cannot grow; without trees no paper. Cloud and paper 'inter-are'.
'Interbeing' is not in the dictionary; 'inter-' plus 'to be' makes the verb 'inter-be'.
Looking deeper: sunshine is in the paper; the logger who cut the tree and brought it to the mill; the wheat that became his daily bread; the logger's father and mother.
Even we are in the paper, because the paper is part of our perception: 'Your mind is in here and mine is also'. Time, space, earth, rain, minerals in the soil, sunshine, cloud, river, heat.

'To be is to inter-be.' 'This sheet of paper is, because everything else is.' Return the sunshine to the sun or the logger to his mother and there is no paper; the sheet is made only of 'non-paper' elements.

Anger: we accept that earthquakes and floods have causes; the person who angered us also has reasons. 'Someone who speaks badly to us may have been spoken to in exactly the same way just the day before, or by his alcoholic father when he was a child.'
Hanh does not say a person who viciously attacks should not be disciplined; first take care of our own seeds of negativity, then act from compassion, not retribution.
scene_details: A sheet of paper with a cloud in it
The logger bringing the tree to the mill, and his daily bread of wheat
Sunshine returned to the sun, logger returned to his mother
tension: A sheet of paper that cannot exist without things that look nothing like paper.
opening_idea: The cloud that is in a sheet of paper, then the logger's bread, then his parents.

lessons.idea: Before judging someone who hurt you, list what stands behind their act as you would list what stands behind a sheet of paper.
lessons.anchor: Cloud, rain, tree, logger, wheat in one sheet; the day before and the childhood behind a harsh word

reflect_final: Think of someone who recently spoke harshly to you: what can you actually name that may have stood behind what they said?

use_cases.move: Ask yourself what the day behind that sentence might have held, then answer the content calmly.

use_cases.situation: A parent repeats a hurtful habit
use_cases.move: Say you want to understand what they grew up with, not to excuse it, then say what you need.

use_cases.situation: You are stewing over a stranger's rude remark
use_cases.move: Hold up any object near you and name three things that had to exist for it to be here; use that pause before reacting.

pocket_idea: Every sheet of paper holds a cloud; every harsh word holds a day you did not see.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: There is a cloud in a sheet of paper, and a logger's bread.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Hanh: no cloud, no rain, no tree, no paper. The logger, his wheat, his parents too. Paper only exists because non-paper does.
